body.transcript:
WEBVTT


00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:02.340
Three days ago, I asked the scrapbook community

00:00:02.341 --> 00:00:05.341
what pages from their baby's first year they love most.

00:00:05.342 --> 00:00:06.621
And now, somehow,

00:00:06.622 --> 00:00:10.701
I accidentally created an entire baby scrapbook planner.

00:00:10.702 --> 00:00:12.581
Yes, you heard that, right?

00:00:12.582 --> 00:00:14.301
It's not just a list anymore.

00:00:14.302 --> 00:00:17.421
It's a full on planner. I already had a list of page ideas

00:00:17.422 --> 00:00:18.661
because I'm trying to finish

00:00:18.662 --> 00:00:21.101
the first six months of my daughter's scrapbook,

00:00:21.102 --> 00:00:23.541
but I knew I had to be missing something.

00:00:23.542 --> 00:00:26.881
So I asked you guys what pages you love most from your books,

00:00:26.882 --> 00:00:30.941
and I got so many amazing suggestions that I hadn't even thought of.

00:00:30.942 --> 00:00:35.721
But what I wasn't expecting was how many of you also needed this list.

00:00:35.722 --> 00:00:37.341
So I took all of these ideas,

00:00:37.342 --> 00:00:39.181
organize everything into category,

00:00:39.182 --> 00:00:41.901
and started building what I thought would just be

00:00:41.902 --> 00:00:44.661
the ultimate list of baby scrapbook page ideas.

00:00:44.662 --> 00:00:47.341
And obviously, my brain just doesn't know when to quit.

00:00:47.342 --> 00:00:49.461
And things got a little bit out of hand again,

00:00:49.462 --> 00:00:52.221
because now it's not even just a list anymore.

00:00:52.222 --> 00:00:55.141
It's a planner. You can go through all of the categories,

00:00:55.142 --> 00:00:57.821
choose the pages that you want in your baby scrapbook,

00:00:57.822 --> 00:01:00.781
and it turns those choices into an organized list

00:01:00.782 --> 00:01:03.601
of what will actually become your book.

00:01:03.602 --> 00:01:05.741
Then you can track which pages you finish,

00:01:05.742 --> 00:01:07.381
what you still need to make them,

00:01:07.382 --> 00:01:11.181
and basically plan your entire baby scrapbook from start to finish.

00:01:11.182 --> 00:01:13.541
So in just three days, we went from, hey,

00:01:13.542 --> 00:01:15.181
what scrapbook pages should I make?

00:01:15.182 --> 00:01:19.201
To an entire baby's first year scrapbook planning system.

00:01:19.280 --> 00:01:23.340
And between these videos, there have already been over 1,000 saves,

00:01:23.341 --> 00:01:25.501
and hundreds of you have followed me,

00:01:25.502 --> 00:01:26.821
waiting for me to share it.

00:01:26.822 --> 00:01:29.461
So I'm officially giving myself a deadline.

00:01:29.462 --> 00:01:33.621
I'm finishing this thing, and I'm dropping it this Saturday.

00:01:33.622 --> 00:01:35.341
So if you want it, follow along,

00:01:35.342 --> 00:01:36.301
because apparently,

00:01:36.302 --> 00:01:39.714
I have two days to finish building a scrapbook planner now.

transcripts.text: If you're a mom who had every intention of creating a baby book for your kid, and then it didn't happen, I have the solution for you. This is the birthday book. My parents did this for me when I was growing up and I have carried the tradition on for my kids simply because it is so easy. Here's the deal, you grab a little scrapbook and then you make a few pages, that's it, to encompass their whole year and you do it on their birthday. So it's kind of like a habit stack for you. Set a little calendar reminder for yourself to print some photos of your baby's year. If you have no clue what photos you want to print, just print the ones that you posted on Instagram because chances are those are your favorites. Then you throw it in your scrapbook. I don't make this perfect by any means, I think messy is honestly cuter. Some fun paper, I write down some of their favorite things, who their friends with, what shows they love right now, their favorite toys. My husband and I each write a little note and that's it. We'll pull that same book out next year and ideally, we'll have 18 years of memories.

Bubby? Bubby? This is my Bubby. A lot of you know her because she shares her memories of her experience in the Holocaust, but there is so much more to her life than just her experience there. For example, there was her childhood before the war, and then after the war when she got married, was building a family, and then all of her memories with her children and grandchildren. We decided to document all of these special memories in book form using Romento. And that picture is my sister, my brother, and me. Bubby is recording her memories of the only surviving photo of her siblings, and Romento will turn her recorded story into a tangible book, and each story will come with a QR code that links to the video recording. When the memory book arrived, my girls' reactions were priceless. Bubby? Bubby? Bubby is 97 years old. I hope and pray that she lives for many more years, but I am so glad she made this book for us. Not only are her memories recorded, but her voice is too. If you have a grandparent, parent, or loved ones whose memories you'd like to preserve, I highly recommend this forever book.

The single most important possession you'll ever have in your life is your personal archive. I save everything. I save most things that people would throw away. I started to realize how much memory fades. Looking back at these physical objects helped me to feel like I wasn't losing the past quite so quickly. One time my dad told me a story about how he convinced his study abroad professor to let him be the captain of a sailboat to do their entire semester class at sea. But in order to do it, he had to get permission from the US Embassy. And as he was telling me the story, I asked him, "Where is the letter where they approved this?" He didn't think that he'd saved it. And I started to cry and he wasn't really sure why and I explained that there's nothing more painful than losing a part of your history. Everything that you save has a story. One day somebody might be looking through those objects piercing together things that they know about you. In my own research and film work, I started to get into a lot of other people's archives. In doing that I couldn't help but think about what was missing. A lot of what we save is the highlights. We save awards, we save, you know, the the glossy pictures. The awards don't tell the story of how you got there. The glossy photos don't tell the story of who you are. It's those other things that we throw away. Those are the things that tell the story of who you are. I interviewed my grandfather. Did an oral history interview with him and I saved that. You know, unfortunately, I didn't realize the importance of all of this until it was too late to interview my grandmothers. I really regret that. The greatest gift that you can give to the people after you is this archive that tells your story.
Hey, your mama ran off and ponder rain. I remember, I remember everything.
